claims.explanation: E01 and evidence/figures/fig2_loss_vs_l2re.md give approximate ranges over PDE/width/optimizer/seed runs, including near-zero-loss trivial solutions with L2RE near 1. C01 combines a monotone nonlinear trend, a PDE-dependent necessity threshold around 1e-5 for low L2RE, and existence of trivial solutions; its falsifier uses a separate L2RE <0.05 and loss >1e-3 condition. No reported-evidence relation expresses this conditional threshold, trend and existential conjunction. A simple optimizer comparison would not preserve C01.

E02 and evidence/figures/fig3_hessian_spectral.md report PDE-specific outlier bounds (>1e4 convection, >1e3 reaction, >1e5 wave), qualitative density near zero, and the ill-conditioning interpretation after 41,000 Adam+L-BFGS iterations. The numeric thresholds are substantive, not merely method labels. Reported relations do not test scalar bounds plus near-zero spectral mass or its effect on first-order convergence. The alternative figure3_hessian_spectral_density.md also provides these bounds and prose, not a fully numerical spectrum.

E02/Figure 3 compares residual, initial-condition and boundary-condition spectra, and C03 additionally asserts theoretical prediction that the differential operator is the source of worst conditioning. figure3_hessian_spectral.md contains convection component approximations and qualitative reaction/wave references; fig3_hessian_spectral.md contains component summaries but fails public evidence parsing at its line-13 separator. Even a largest-eigenvalue comparison would not express the theoretical/source-of-conditioning conjunct or equate top eigenvalue with a condition number without the remaining spectrum.

The full assertion is a >=1000-fold top-eigenvalue reduction for each of three PDEs and every loss component, despite the weaker 100-fold falsifier. evidence/figures/fig3_hessian_spectral.md contains total and component summaries for all PDEs, but public aratest evidence parsing fails at line 13 because '|--|--|--|' is not an accepted separator. The alternate figure3_hessian_spectral.md has bound/range strings and only convection component numbers, with reaction/wave components summarized qualitatively; figure3_hessian_spectral_density.md is also incomplete for these operands. The >=1000 ratio relation is available, but a usable complete evidence grid is not. Evidence was not edited or replaced by invented values.

Table 1 (evidence/tables/table1_optimizer_comparison.md) gives minima selected across widths, learning rates and switch points, not separate results for every width 50/100/200/400. Figure 8 (figure8_optimizer_comparison.md) supplies qualitative winners and reaction exceptions at width 100 for loss and 200 for L2RE, but no width-resolved loss/L2RE measurements. A best-baseline relation on Table 1 would silently replace the all-width assertion with a best-over-widths assertion and ignore its conjunction with the stated 14.2x and 6.07x improvements. The observed exceptions are retained rather than removed from scope.

E04 and Table 2 (table2_nncg_results.md) identify the best-L2RE Adam+L-BFGS starts and 2,000-step NNCG/GD continuations; Table 3 (table3_timing.md) reports per-iteration seconds. The complete claim requires strictly >10-fold loss reduction, L2RE improvement on all PDEs, zero GD improvement, and the stated 5–322-fold timing range. Reported-evidence relations support inclusive ratio_ge/ratio_le but not a strict ratio threshold (>10), while ordinary gt compares unscaled measurements. Replacing >10 by >=10 or the weaker >2 falsifier would alter the assertion; no such repair was made. Loss-versus-L2RE start selection and the different reaction loss in Table 1 were not conflated.

C07 asserts Theorem 8.4's high-probability asymptotic lower bound under eigenvalue-decay alpha >1/2 and residual-sample assumptions. E05 and evidence/figures/figure10_condition_number.md describe an empirical proxy lambda1/lambda129 for a two-layer width-32 convection model; figure rows contain 'low', 'moderate' and 'highest', not numeric condition numbers. A finite monotonicity comparison, even with additional measurements, would not establish the quantified asymptotic theorem or its probability and assumptions. No fresh experiment was proposed as a substitute proof.
